pages.text: Is a dead universe dead forever? Statistical mechanics says no. In a finite system every state recurs (Poincaré recurrence) - for a de Sitter universe after about e^{10¹²²} years. Long before that, fluctuations happen by chance: P ∝ exp(−(Δ_E − TΔ_S)/k_BT). A single brain is far more likely than a whole world - the $(thing)Boltzmann brain$() problem.
The $(item)Entropy Horizon$() waits for one: a horizon shard and negentropy in the haze give a $(item)Boltzmann Fluctuation$() - which a Psionic Resonator turns into two $(item)Boltzmann Brains$().
And the other way out is $(thing)Conformal Cyclic Cosmology$() (in Strings & the Multiverse): the end of one aeon is the beginning of the next.
